The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party in Katsina State, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke, has promised to introduce free healthcare services for residents if elected governor in the 2027 governorship election. Lado made the pledge on Saturday during the inauguration of a 2,000-member governorship campaign council at the party’s state secretariat in Katsina. He said his administration would prioritise healthcare, education and security, which he described as critical sectors that had suffered setbacks under the present administration. The former senator assured residents that access to medical services would not be determined by their financial capacity, promising that patients would receive treatment in hospitals without out-of-pocket payments. “I will not allow anyone who is sick to pay a penny in hospital if elected governor come 2027,” he declared. He expressed concern over what he described as declining standards in the education sector, while accusing the government of failing to adequately address the security challenges confronting communities across the state. “In the last three years, education has suffered a setback in Katsina State. Insecurity is also another concern bedevilling the state, which we got into due to poor administration in the last three years,” he said. 2027: I can’t work against Tinubu – Oriyomi Hamzat 2027: Adebutu hails Wike after court restores candidacy 2027: Obi, Atiku handing victory to APC — Lamido The PDP candidate, however, promised to adopt a different development approach if elected, saying he would work with his team to improve the state’s fortunes. “We will change the narrative if given the mandate. With my team, Insha Allah, Katsina will become an enviable state in the federation,” he added. Earlier, the state PDP Chairman, Nura Amadi, said the composition of the 2,000-member campaign council reflected the party’s determination to win the 2027 governorship election. Amadi expressed confidence in the calibre and diversity of the council members, noting that they included captains of industry, retired civil servants, former security personnel, students and women, among other groups. “With the calibre of individuals in this committee, PDP will no doubt emerge victorious come 2027,” he said. He urged members of the various committees to demonstrate commitment, strengthen grassroots mobilisation and work collectively towards achieving the party’s electoral ambition. Retired Brigadier-General Sagir Musa was also named as a member of the team to help coordinate the PDP governorship campaign council. Faith Maji
